sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Enhancement"][color=shaman]Enhancement Shaman Rotation in Midnight[/color][/h2]
[pad]

Even with the reduction in complexity after the Midnight changes, Enhancement Shaman can be a little overwhelming at first glance. Since it has more active buttons than the average spec, it means there's a bit of a learning curve when trying to understand how it all comes together. To start, we'll go over some core rules, which will help get you up to speed quickly with your rotational goals. These are listed in order of importance:

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=shaman][icon name=spell_fire_elementaldevastation type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon] Enhancement Shaman Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]
[pad]

While Enhancement's cooldown tools are still skinny in Midnight, the options available still pack a punch going into Season 2. Making use of them properly is a little more involved than many specializations, since they don't function as flat increases and instead modify the rotation. The below sections cover [i]how[/i] each cooldown works, and how to get the most out of each use.

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Doom Winds" icon=ability_ironmaidens_swirlingvortex]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_ironmaidens_swirlingvortex type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Doom Winds[/color][/h3]
[pad]
[wrapper width=98%]
[spell=384352] is your standard cooldown choice, with a 1-minute cooldown and 8-second duration baseline (increasing to 10 with [spell=384444] taken) - while also being [b]off the GCD[/b]. While active, your chance to trigger [spell=33757] is increasted by 50% ([i]multiplicative of your base change, [b]not[/b] additive[/i]) Additionally, all Windfury Weapon damage you deal while it's active is increased by 20%. This [b]does not[/b] impact the bonus attacks from [spell=462854].

Important things to know are:
[ul]
[li]While Doom Winds is active, [b]Main-Hand[/b] special attacks rise in value, as they can trigger a Windfury Weapon bonus attack.
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right][i]Main Hand Strikes are: [spell=17364] / [spell=115356], [spell=187874], [spell=197214] / [spell=445035] and all 3 [spell=1218047] strikes.[/i][/li]
[/ul]
[/li]
[li]Each enemy hit by the [b]initial cast[/b] of Crash Lightning, and any target hit by Sundering (or Splitstream) count as Main-Hand strikes on each [i]individual[/i] target, providing "AoE Windfury procs". Since Doom Winds increases this chance significantly, it grants truly uncapped AoE when active.[/li]
[li]When playing with Primordial Storm, this should always be synced with Doom Winds casts - it provides 3 individual AoE Windfury triggers,[/li]
[/ul]

In Midnight this [i]also[/i] gains the effects of both [spell=384411] and [spell=384444] while active, if taken. The former generates 1/2 stacks of [spell=187880] every second, while the latter gives a way to spend resources through both Stormstrike and Crash Lightning. We go into further detail on how this works in its respective tab.

[minor-heading type=bar toc=false] [symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color] Doom Winds[/minor-heading]
[pad]
[b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color][/b] always plays with Doom Winds as its cooldown, as it naturally lines up with [spell=444995]. This window is perfect to overlap with your [spell=201900] triggers, as it allows you to generate a huge surplus of Maelstrom Weapon through Static Accumulation, and spend it efficiently through Thorim's Invocation. This, in turn, extends the buff for a significant duration with [spell=1260644], and is a core part of its Midnight cooldown rotation. While active, it has a few simple rules:

[ul]
[li][b]Always[/b] weave [spell=60103] on cooldown during this, making sure Hot Hand has been triggered from [spell=453405].[/li]
[li][b]Cast Activators[/b] in between. Priority is Crash Lightning \u279c Stormstrike, which should provide cooldown reduction through [spell=1250364].[/li]
[/ul]
[pad]
[/wrapper]
[hr]
[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Ascendance" icon=spell_fire_elementaldevastation]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_fire_elementaldevastation type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Ascendance[/color][/h3]
[pad]
[wrapper width=98%]

[spell=114051] and [spell=378270] is a choice node capstone, which [i]replaces[/i] [spell=384352] when taken. When triggered, you're transformed into an air ascendant, converting your [spell=17364] into [spell=115356] and auto-attacks into [spell=114089]. Both of these attacks have a 30-yard range, are considered special attacks, and ignore your target's armor. Additionally, Windstrike gains the benefit of any talent that benefits Stormstrike, and its cooldown is reduced by 60% while active. Depending on which talent is taken, there's a few different things to know:
[hr]
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b]Ascendance –[/b] Has a 3-minute cooldown, reduced to 2 minutes by [spell=384444], and lasts for 15 seconds. When activated, Doom Winds is triggered at the same time for 10 seconds. Finally, whenever you spend [spell=187880] [i]outside[/i] of this form, there's a 0.5% chance per stack to trigger Doom Winds.[hr][/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b]Deeply Rooted Elements –[/b] Provides a 0.6% chance per stack of Maelstrom Weapon spent to trigger Ascendance for 8 seconds [i]and[/i] Doom Winds for 10 seconds.[/li]
[/ul]
[hr]

Both these [i]also[/i] gain the effects of both [spell=384411] and Thorim's Invocation while active, if taken. The former generates 1/2 stacks of [spell=187880] every second, while the latter gives a way to spend resources through both Windstrike and [spell=187874]. We go into further detail on how this works in its respective tab. These talents are [i]always[/i] taken in conjunction with this node, and turns the window into a race to cast Windstrike as much as possible when active.

Both of these effects work on a [b]Deck of Cards[/b] proc system, meaning the chance to trigger it has an upper (and lower) limit. If you're unaware of how these work, you can click the toggler below for a brief rundown.

[wrapper width=70%][pad][pad]
[center][large][b][toggler id="DOC" hidden][icon name=inv_111_gallyjack_gallywix size=small type=round inline=true color=c7][/icon] [color=shaman]What is a "Deck of Cards" Proc System?[/color][/toggler][/b][/large][/center]
[/wrapper]
[div id="DOC" hidden]
[pad]
[hr]

[wrapper width=90%]
[span style="background-color: #202020; color: #ededed; position: relative; top: 15px; left: 35px; padding: 2px 6px; line-height: 1; border-radius: 4px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0px;"]
[icon name=inv_111_gallyjack_gallywix size=small type=round inline=true color=c7][/icon] [large][color=q6]Deck of Cards procs Explained[/color][/large][/span]
[center]
[div style="border:2px solid #2788e6; padding:14px; border-radius:10px;"]
[pad]
Deck of Cards systems are used on specific abilities with the goal of limiting how much you can lowroll (or highroll) certain effects. The way they work is fairly similar to the namesake:

A "deck" of potential opportunities to proc an effect will be assigned - for example's sake 100 - and each time you activate the trigger, one "card" will be drawn. Of this "deck" of 100, any number of "cards" - for this example two - are assigned as a trigger, granting the effect. Every time you cycle through all 100 "cards" by activating the trigger, the "deck" will reset and a new deck of 100 will begin, with 2 randomly assigned new trigger cards inside it.

Currently, [spell=1262713], [spell=454009], [spell=378270] and [spell=384352] triggered through the [spell=114051] talent all function on these systems. Since [spell=187880] spent to cycle the deck isn't fixed, instead each individual stack is batched in 10 (with no two cards being less than 10 stacks apart).

[/div]
[/center]
[/wrapper]
[pad]
[hr]

[pad]
[/div][pad][pad]

[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][symbol=wow-hero-talent-stormbringer] [color=shaman][color=q9]Stormbringer[/color] Ascendance[/color][/minor-heading]
[pad]
Due to the heavy Maelstrom Weapon generation while active, [symbol=wow-hero-talent-stormbringer] [b][color=q9]Stormbringer[/color][/b] can often find it struggles to drain it off with Thorim's Invocation triggers alone. Especially with [spell=1262635] and [spell=455110] refunds considered, it will often lead to situations where you overcap, but there's no way of draining it faster. In Midnight, Thorim's Invocation [i]always[/i] spends up to 10 stacks with [spell=384149] taken, so just cast it on cooldown. In [b]both Single-target and AoE, it follows these rules:[/b]:

[ul]
[li]Cast Crash Lightning as a priority, and Windstrike otherwise. Even if [spell=454009] procs, trigger it with Thorim's as normal.[/li]
[/ul]
[pad]
[/wrapper]
[hr]
[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Thorim's Invocation" icon=spell_shaman_ancestralawakening]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_shaman_ancestralawakening type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Thorim's Invocation[/color][/h3]
[pad]
[wrapper width=98%]

In Midnight, we have multiple ways of triggering [spell=384444] - both through [spell=114051] like before, [i]and[/i] through [spell=384352]. This is an exceptionally powerful effect, allowing us to siphon our [spell=187880] through other GCDs that generate it, condensing two casts into one. When paired with [spell=384411] granting generation every second during these windows, it leads to explosive cooldown power, high burst, and an overflow of resources. The basic function is:

[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b]Mechanics –[/b] Whenever you cast specific abilities, up to [b]5[/b] Maelstrom Weapon (or up to [b]10[/b] with [spell=384149]) will be consumed to discharge either [spell=188196], [spell=454009] if active, or [spell=188443]. This is activated by:[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b]Doom Winds –[/b] Casting [spell=17364] or [spell=187874] discharges a spender.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b]Ascendance –[/b] Casting [spell=115356] or [spell=187874] discharges a spender.[/li]
[/ul]

[hr]

The Maelstrom Weapon spender cast is dictated by a few conditions, and setting it to an ability is known as [b]"TI Priming"[/b]. This works as follows:
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b]Lightning Bolt / Chain Lightning Casts –[/b] primes Thorim's Invocation to each respective spell.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b]Tempest Casts –[/b] [i]Dynamic[/i]: If it hits one target, switches to Lightning, two or more switches to Chain Lightning.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b][spell=1218047] Casts –[/b] [i]Dynamic[/i]: primes to Lightning Bolt / Chain Lightning depending on targets hit with the preceding strikes.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b][spell=204357] Procs -[/b] [i]Do not[/i] influence priming in any way.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-stormbringer] [color=q9]Stormbringer[/color] -[/b] with Tempest active, it will [i]always[/i] be consumed, regardless of the current priming state.[/li]
[/ul]

In Midnight, it's good to know what you're currently primed to, but with the removal of addons it's quite difficult to know for sure. You already want to be in the correct state [i]before[/i] you cast these, as fixing it while they're active forces you to use up a valuable GCD on the appropriate spell. Both Hero Trees open with an ability that has dynamic priming after starting cooldowns though, which often fixes the problem - [b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-stormbringer] [color=q9]Stormbringer[/color][/b] casts Tempest via [spell=1264688], and [b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color][/b] casts Primordial Storm almost immediately after starting the window.

[pad]
[/wrapper]
[hr]
[pad]
[/tab]


[tab name="Sundering" icon=ability_rhyolith_lavapool]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_rhyolith_lavapool type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Sundering[/color][/h3]
[pad]

In Midnight, [spell=197214] takes the place on the tree as your mid cooldown burst tool, and inherits the same follow-up talents and bonuses that [spell=375982] did previously. It comes with a 30-second cooldown (and [i]no longer incapacitates[/i]), and deals a large amount of direct Flamestrike damage to targets in a line in front of you. These hits [i]can[/i] trigger weapon imbues, including [spell=33757]. This is a staple talent in all [b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color][/b] builds due to [spell=445024], but also flexes as a high damage burst AoE button.

[spell=382042] causes Sundering casts to grant 15% Haste for 12 seconds whenever cast, and also generates 5 [spell=187880] instantly. This is often layered over other cooldowns, and the extra resources it grants makes it an excellent setup tool as well. Note - this [b][i]does not[/i][/b] trigger from [spell=445035] as [b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color][/b].

Casting Sundering with [spell=1218047] taken grants a 15-second buff window, replacing the keybind with a powerful 4-step AoE attack. When cast, this consumes (and scales) with all current Maelstrom Stacks, and deals a series of attacks in a fixed order [color=unfriendly]Fire[/color] \u279c [color=kyrian]Frost[/color] \u279c [color=hunter]Nature[/color] \u279c [spell=188196] / [spell=188443]. Each of the first three elemental strikes are considered AoE Main-Hand hits (so can trigger Windfury separately), and it then selects Lightning Bolt or Chain Lightning, based on the number of targets hit by the initial strikes. Note - this is [i]not[/i] activated by Splitstream as [b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color][/b].

[pad]
[hr]

Depending on the Hero Talent tree taken, the ability serves a variety of functions, but we always aim to use it on cooldown every 30 seconds:

[ul]
[li][symbol=wow-hero-talent-stormbringer] [b][color=q9]Stormbringer[/color] –[/b] makes use of this as a strong front-loaded burst cooldown in AoE situations, using the Haste provided by Surging Elements to empower [spell=114051]. Unfortunately, it struggles to fit it into single target builds.[/li]
[li][symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [b][color=venthyr]Totemic[/color] –[/b] [i]always[/i] takes this due to interactions with Whirling Elements. The additional Haste it can layer over both [spell=444995] and [spell=384352] consistently makes an already strong combo of cooldowns even more powerful.[/li]
